subject: Critical Thinking
title: Care Ethics: Relationships as the Foundation of Morality
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Care Ethics: Relationships as the Foundation of Morality.

hook.text: A mother doesn't save her child because of a 'universal moral law.' She does it because she loves them.

buildup.text: Care ethics: morality is rooted in relationships, empathy, & responsiveness to others' needs – not abstract principles.

discovery.text: Gilligan argued traditional ethics was male-biased: focused on justice & rules while ignoring care, context, &.

twist.text: Critics: if morality is about caring for those close to you, what about distant strangers?

climax.text: The synthesis: care AND justice are both needed. Care without justice is favoritism.

punchline.text: Morality isn't just rules. It's also showing up for people. Both matter.

quiz.question: What does care ethics argue is the foundation of morality?
options: Relationships, empathy, and responsiveness to others' needs

details.summary: Care ethics grounds morality in relationships, empathy, and responsiveness to the needs of others rather than abstract principles. It arose partly as a feminist critique of rule-based systems that ignore emotional context.
details.whyItMatters: Care ethics highlights moral dimensions that rights-based and utilitarian frameworks overlook, especially in caregiving and personal relationships.
takeaways: Relationships and empathy are central to moral reasoning
Context matters more than abstract universal rules
Care ethics emerged from feminist philosophy

faq.question: How does care ethics challenge traditional ethical theories?
faq.answer: Traditional theories emphasize impartial rules or consequences. Care ethics argues that partiality—caring more for those close to you—is not a flaw but a moral strength.

faq.question: Is care ethics only relevant to personal relationships?
faq.answer: No. It extends to public policy, healthcare, education, and any domain where attentiveness to individual needs and power dynamics matters.
